project.name: CampusCare
project.full_title: CampusCare - Campus Complaint & Issue Management System

project.one_sentence_description: A web application where students submit campus-related complaints and track their progress, while authorized administrators review, update, and resolve those complaints.
project.problem_statement: Students need a centralized way to report university-related problems and know whether those problems are being addressed. Administrators need one place to review, organize, prioritize, and update reported issues.
project.solution_statement: CampusCare provides student and administrator interfaces connected to a Node.js and Express backend and a MongoDB database. Students can create and track their own complaints; administrators can manage all complaints and record status updates and remarks.
primary_goals: Provide a clear form for students to submit campus complaints.
Allow students to view and track the status of their own complaints.
Allow administrators to view and manage complaints from all students.
Keep complaint records in a persistent database.
Protect accounts and restrict actions according to the logged-in user's role.
Demonstrate the frontend-to-backend-to-database flow expected in a full-stack project.

mvp_in_scope: Administrator login using an account created through a controlled seed/manual setup process.
Student dashboard showing the student's own complaints.
Complaint submission with title, description, category, and optional location.
Complaint detail view and status tracking.
Student editing/deletion only while a complaint is in Pending status.
Admin filtering by status and category.
Admin status updates and optional administrative remarks.
Basic dashboard counts for total, pending, in-progress, resolved, and rejected complaints.
Input validation, authentication, role-based authorization, and centralized error handling.

Complex workflow approvals across several departments.
Public complaint visibility or public user profiles.

future_enhancements: AI-assisted complaint category suggestion using a Generative AI API.
RAG-based answers from an approved campus FAQ or policy document collection.
Email notifications when complaint status changes.
Image attachment support with file-type and file-size validation.
Complaint activity timeline and admin audit log.
scope.scope_control_rule: Finish and test the MVP before starting any future enhancement. Do not add a new feature unless the team has time to test and document it.

roles.description: A registered student who can submit and track personal complaints.
permissions: View only complaints created by that student.
View the detail of an owned complaint.
Edit an owned complaint only when its status is Pending.
Delete an owned complaint only when its status is Pending.
Not permitted to change complaint status or admin remarks.

roles.description: An authorized administrator who manages campus complaints.
permissions: View complaint details and student-submitted information needed to process the issue.
Add or update an administrative remark.
Not permitted to create another admin through public registration.

authorization_rules: The backend must verify the JWT before protected endpoints execute.
The backend must check the user's role for admin-only endpoints.
The backend must check complaint ownership for student detail, update, and delete operations.
Never rely only on hiding frontend buttons for access control.
Public registration must always assign the student role; admin creation must be controlled by a seed script or direct authorized setup.

functional_requirements.name: Student registration
functional_requirements.description: Allow a student to create an account using name, email, and password.
acceptance_criteria: Name, email, and password are required.
Email is normalized and must be unique.
Password is stored only as a bcrypt/bcryptjs hash, never as plain text.
Public registration creates a student role only.
Invalid input returns a clear validation response.

functional_requirements.name: Login and authentication
functional_requirements.description: Authenticate registered users and issue a signed JWT.
acceptance_criteria: Correct credentials allow login.
Incorrect credentials return a generic authentication error.
The response does not expose the password hash.
Protected endpoints reject missing, invalid, or expired tokens.

functional_requirements.name: Create complaint
functional_requirements.description: Allow a logged-in student to submit a campus issue.
acceptance_criteria: Title, description, and category are required.
Location is optional.
The backend assigns the complaint owner from the authenticated user, not from a client-supplied user ID.
New complaints start with Pending status.
Creation time and update time are recorded.

functional_requirements.name: List complaints
functional_requirements.description: Return complaints according to the authenticated user's role.
acceptance_criteria: Students receive only their own complaints.
Admins receive all complaints.
The endpoint supports optional status and category filters.
The endpoint uses a consistent JSON response format.

functional_requirements.name: View complaint details
functional_requirements.description: Return one complaint to an authorized user.
acceptance_criteria: The complaint ID must be valid.
A student can access only their own complaint.
An admin can access any complaint.
A missing complaint returns HTTP 404.

functional_requirements.name: Edit complaint
functional_requirements.description: Allow the complaint owner to edit eligible fields before an administrator begins processing it.
acceptance_criteria: Only the complaint owner can edit it as a student.
Only Pending complaints can be edited by students.
The student cannot edit status, owner, or admin remarks.
Invalid fields are rejected.

functional_requirements.name: Delete complaint
functional_requirements.description: Allow the complaint owner to remove an unprocessed complaint.
acceptance_criteria: Only the complaint owner can delete it as a student.
Only Pending complaints can be deleted by students.
Deletion returns a clear success response.

functional_requirements.name: Admin complaint management
functional_requirements.description: Allow an administrator to process complaints and record status and remarks.
acceptance_criteria: Only admins can use the status update endpoint.
Status must be one of the allowed values.
Admin remark is optional and length-limited.
The system updates the complaint updatedAt timestamp.

functional_requirements.name: Dashboard statistics
functional_requirements.description: Show aggregate complaint counts to the administrator.
acceptance_criteria: Only admins can access aggregate statistics.
Counts match the complaints stored in the database.
The dashboard handles zero complaints without errors.

functional_requirements.name: Filtering and search
functional_requirements.description: Help users locate complaints by status and category, and optionally by title text.
acceptance_criteria: Filters are validated and do not bypass authorization.
Student filters apply only to the student's own complaints.
Admin filters apply to the admin's authorized complaint list.

non_functional_requirements: Usability: pages should have clear labels, helpful validation messages, and consistent navigation.
Responsive design: the main pages should work on laptop and mobile-sized screens.
Security: passwords must be hashed; secrets must be stored in environment variables; endpoints must enforce authentication and authorization.
Maintainability: use separate routes, controllers, models, middleware, and configuration files.
Reliability: handle invalid requests and database/server errors without crashing the application.
Performance: use database queries and filters rather than downloading every record when the complaint list grows; pagination can be added after the basic list works.
Accessibility: use semantic HTML, visible focus states, form labels, and sufficient text contrast.
Portability: document local setup and deployment configuration in README.md.
business_rules: New complaints are assigned Pending status by the backend.
Allowed statuses are Pending, In Progress, Resolved, and Rejected.
Allowed categories are Classroom, Internet/Wi-Fi, Hostel, Library, Transport, Maintenance, and Other.
A student can see only their own complaints.
A student can edit or delete only their own Pending complaints.
Only an admin can change status or add an admin remark.
The client must not decide complaint ownership; the authenticated server-side user determines createdBy.
A public registration request cannot set role to admin.

frontend.purpose: Layout, responsive styling, and visual design
Form handling, validation, fetch requests, and dynamic dashboard rendering

backend.purpose: Routing, middleware, REST API, and static frontend serving
MongoDB schemas, validation, references, and queries

developer_tools.purpose: Containerization learning and repeatable local setup; add after MVP

deployment_target.recommended_project_arrangement: Deploy the Express application on a Node.js-capable host such as Render or Railway and use a MongoDB database service. Verify the current provider plan, limits, and deployment instructions before deploying.
deployment_target.database: MongoDB Atlas or another MongoDB-compatible hosted database
deployment_target.note: The syllabus lists Render, Vercel, and Railway as deployment examples. This specification does not promise that any provider currently offers a free plan.

technology_stack.frontend_framework_decision: Use plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the first version. React is intentionally excluded to keep the project aligned with the team's selected frontend and reduce additional learning overhead.

syllabus_alignment.course_perspective: The course emphasizes hands-on design, development, testing, and deployment of full-stack backend applications; RESTful APIs with Node.js and Express; database integration such as MongoDB; secure authentication; production-ready backend code; Generative AI APIs and RAG; Docker; and cloud deployment.

course_outcomes.statement: Building server-side applications using Node.js and Express.
course_outcomes.campuscare_evidence: Express server, modular backend, middleware, and API endpoints.

course_outcomes.statement: Designing and developing RESTful APIs for web-based solutions.
course_outcomes.campuscare_evidence: Complaint and authentication REST endpoints using HTTP methods and status codes.

course_outcomes.statement: Integrating backend systems with databases for data persistence.
course_outcomes.campuscare_evidence: Mongoose models, MongoDB connection, references, queries, and persistent complaints/users.

course_outcomes.statement: Implementing authentication, authorization, and middleware in backend applications.
course_outcomes.campuscare_evidence: JWT verification, bcrypt password hashing, protected routes, and student/admin role middleware.

units.title: Express.js and REST API Development

Routing: static/dynamic routes and route parameters
Middleware concepts: built-in, custom, and error-handling
Controllers, routers, and modular structure for scaling apps
Express Generator and folder best practices
REST principles: statelessness, resources, and HTTP verbs
Full CRUD API: POST and GET; PUT/PATCH and DELETE
Error handling using try-catch, centralized middleware, and status codes
Building and testing APIs using Postman
campuscare_work: Create separate authentication and complaint routers.
Create controllers for request handling.
Use route parameters such as complaint IDs.
Implement create, read, update, and delete operations.
Create authentication, role, and error middleware.
Test endpoints with Postman and record example requests/responses.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to databases: SQL vs NoSQL and MongoDB setup
Data modeling with Mongoose or Sequelize
Schema design, validations, and references
Querying and populating: find(), populate(), and aggregation basics
Real-time data flow with full database CRUD integration
Authentication basics: password hashing with bcrypt
Token-based authentication: JWT setup, signing, and verification
Protecting routes with role-based middleware
Environment variables with dotenv and secret management
Best practices for securing credentials and APIs
campuscare_work: Create User and Complaint Mongoose schemas.
Reference the complaint creator using a Mongoose ObjectId.
Use find(), findById(), update operations, and populate() where useful.
Hash passwords and verify them during login.
Create and verify JWTs.
Enforce role and ownership restrictions in backend middleware/controllers.
Load secrets and connection strings from environment variables.

units.title: AI, Design and Deployment
syllabus_topics: Low-Level Design (LLD): modularity, SOLID principles, and code reuse

Write automated tests for health, authentication, and complaint permissions.
Complete deployment and document environment variables.

Add Dockerfile and Compose configuration as a later learning milestone.

learning_experiences_to_include: Hands-on lab sessions: REST APIs, CRUD, middleware, and authentication workflows using Node.js and Express.
Code walkthroughs and debugging: explain routing, middleware flow, error handling, and debugging techniques.
Project-based learning: build the system in stages from routing to database integration and deployment.
Live demonstrations: Postman, MongoDB Compass, JWT, and session management concepts.
Peer reviews: review backend structure, security, and API design.
Outside-class practice: GitHub collaboration, cloud deployment, environment variables, and basic CI/CD concepts.
Portfolio building: publish a README and API documentation with the project.

collections.name: users

notes: Never accept admin role from public registration.

collections.name: complaints

fields.name: createdBy
fields.rules: Set from authenticated user on the server.

fields.name: adminRemark
fields.rules: Only admins can set/update; suggested maximum length 1000 characters.

indexes: Index createdBy for student complaint queries
Index status and category for admin filtering
relationships: Each complaint belongs to one user through createdBy.

response_convention.rule: Use the same outer response shape across endpoints. Do not include password hashes, secrets, or stack traces in client responses.

api_design.authentication: Protected endpoints require a valid JWT. The server must identify the user from the verified token. Do not trust a user ID or role supplied in the request body.

endpoints.purpose: Authenticate a user and issue a JWT.
Return safe details of the currently authenticated user.
List complaints. Students receive their own; admins receive all. Optional query filters: status, category, page, limit.
Get one complaint after ownership/role verification.
Edit allowed complaint fields while status is Pending.
Delete a complaint while status is Pending.
Update status and optional admin remark.
Return total and per-status complaint counts.

http_status_guidance.404: Requested resource does not exist or is not available to that user, according to the chosen privacy policy.

security_rules: Use a long, randomly generated JWT secret outside example files.
Do not paste real credentials into source code, GitHub issues, screenshots, or chat messages.
Use a separate database and secret for deployment.
Never log passwords, JWTs, or database connection strings.

local_setup_guide.assumed_environment: Windows laptop with VS Code and Node.js installed; commands are shown for Command Prompt and PowerShell where they differ.

steps.action: Download and extract the CampusCare starter folder.
Open the extracted CampusCare folder in VS Code using File > Open Folder.
Open VS Code Terminal > New Terminal and confirm the terminal is in the project folder.
Create a local environment file. Edit the values for the database and JWT secret.
Start the development server using the package script.
Open the homepage in a browser.
Verify that the health endpoint returns a success JSON response.

troubleshooting.check: Verify Node.js and npm installation and restart the terminal.
Stop the other process or change PORT in .env.
Confirm MongoDB is running or the Atlas URI and network access are configured. The server should report a clear connection error.
Use the same CommonJS or ES module syntax consistently and verify package.json configuration.
Confirm nodemon is running, save the file, and refresh the browser.

workflow: Pull the latest develop branch before starting a task.
Create a feature branch for the task.
Run the relevant tests and check the application locally.
Push the branch and open a pull request into develop.
Ask another member to review the changes.
Resolve feedback and merge only after checks pass.

manual_postman_scenarios: Student registration succeeds with valid details.
Login succeeds with correct credentials and fails with incorrect credentials.
Protected endpoint rejects a missing token.
Student sees only their own complaints.
Student cannot access another student's complaint by changing the ID.
Student cannot update status or admin remark.
Student can edit/delete an owned Pending complaint.
Student cannot edit/delete a complaint after it is no longer Pending.
Admin can view all complaints and update status.
Invalid category/status and missing required fields are rejected.
automated_test_targets: Registration validation and password hashing behavior.
definition_of_done_for_a_feature: Input validation and error handling are included.
Authorization is checked on the backend where applicable.
The feature is tested manually or automatically.
The code is committed to a feature branch and reviewed.
The feature is documented if it changes the API or setup.

mandatory_controls: Hash passwords with bcrypt/bcryptjs; never store plain-text passwords.
Use JWT verification middleware for protected routes.
Check roles and resource ownership on the server.
Prevent public users from assigning themselves the admin role.
Validate and sanitize request fields and allowed enum values.
Keep database URI and JWT secret in environment variables.
Do not return password hashes, tokens, environment values, or stack traces in error responses.
Use Helmet and sensible request logging; do not log secrets or credentials.
Restrict deployed database access and use a separate production secret.
security_and_quality.student_project_caveat: This is an educational semester project. A production university deployment would need a fuller security review, secure token storage strategy, audit logging, operational monitoring, backups, and institution-approved data handling.

suggested_demo_sequence: Introduce the real campus problem and explain the purpose of CampusCare.
Show a student registering and logging in.
Submit a complaint with a category and location.

Show Postman tests, README, GitHub history, and deployment if available.
